newsitem.title: CANADA: Another Canada firm signs U.S. Indian oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Another Canada firm signs U.S. Indian oil deal.

text.p: Junior oil company K2 Energy Corp on Monday joined a growing number of Canadian companies in inking a deal to explore for oil on Indian lands in the northern United States.
Calgary-based K2 said it signed an exploration and development agreement with the Blackfeet Indian Tribe in northern Montana covering three areas totaling 285,000 acres.
The company said it selected the Blackfeet Reservation lands using both aeromagnetic and a new advanced Russian inertial gravity meter system.

Earlier this year, Alberta Energy Co Ltd signed an oil exploration deal with the Mandan, Hidatsa and Arkidara tribes in North Dakota. Gulf Canada Resources Ltd negotiated an agreement in December with the Sioux and Assiniboine tribes in Montana, giving it access to 110,000 acres of lands in that state.
K2 said its lands, which are just across the Canada-U.S. border from sought-after oil and gas acreage in southern Alberta, were virtually unexplored with less than one well per 23,000 acres.
The company said it was preparing an exploration program and planned to drill several wells on the lands before the end of the year.
